ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rhombus $ABCD$, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$. If $AB=3$ and $BD=4$, what is the area of rhombus $ABCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus and $BD=4$,\\
it follows that $OB=2$,\\
Since $AB=3$,\\
we have $OA=\sqrt{AB^{2}-OB^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}-2^{2}}=\sqrt{5}$,\\
Therefore, $AC=2OA=2\sqrt{5}$,\\
So, the area of rhombus $ABCD$ is $S_{\text{rhombus}ABCD}=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BD=\frac{1}{2}\times 2\sqrt{5}\times 4=4\sqrt{5}$,\\
Hence, the answer is: $S_{\text{rhombus}ABCD}=\boxed{4\sqrt{5}}$.

By the Pythagorean theorem, OA=√(AB²-OB²)=√(3²-2²)=√5. Therefore AC=2OA=2√5. The area of a rhombus equals half the product of the two diagonals, so the area = (1/2)×AC×BD = (1/2)×2√5×4 = 4√5.
